headlines: A TEN FOOT SEA LEVEL RISE WOULD SUBMERGE LOW MIAMI BEACH STREETS
TEN FEET HIGHER: WHAT HAPPENS TO MIAMI BEACH
CAN MIAMI DEFENSES SURVIVE TEN FEET OF RISING OCEAN WATER
posts.article: A hypothetical ten-foot rise in ocean levels would put low streets across Miami Beach beneath everyday tides. Situated between the Atlantic Ocean and Biscayne Bay, low-lying ground would stay underwater without massive defensive upgrades. Seawalls alone cannot prevent flooding because South Florida rests on porous limestone, which lets rising groundwater bubble up from underneath. This rising water table compromises septic systems that require dry soil to process waste. Miami-Dade is already converting vulnerable septic tanks to sewer lines in Little River, working to protect communities and the Biscayne aquifer that provides our drinking water.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE BREAKS ANNUAL RECORD WITH 24 HOMES SOLD ABOVE 30 MILLION DOLLARS
MIAMI ULTRA-LUXURY REAL ESTATE SHATTERS ALL-TIME SALES RECORDS
WHY BILLIONAIRES CANNOT STOP BUYING MULTI-MILLION-DOLLAR MIAMI ESTATES THIS YEAR
posts.article:
Miami-Dade County has broken its all-time annual record for ultra-luxury residential sales in just the first nine months of 2026. Buyers closed on 24 single-family houses and condominiums priced at $30 million or higher through September, surpassing the previous full-year record of 21 transactions set in 2025.

Market tracking by MIAMI REALTORS and RWorld indicates the county could reach 32 mega-deals by year end. While wealthy purchasers fueled record high-end activity, overall county residential sales dropped two percent in September to 1,733 closings as borrowing costs climbed, with mortgage rates reaching 7.46 percent in October. Still, local single-family median prices rose over four percent to $692,000.
